history.summary: An ancient temple dedicated to Goddess Bhagavati in her Ashtabhuja (eight-armed) form, an incarnation of Durga, standing on a high pedestal. It is one of the few Goa temples said to have survived Portuguese rule. The complex has five shrines: the main Bhagavati temple plus Shri Sateri, Shri Dev Ravalnath, Shri Dev Bhivangi Panchakshari and Brahma (with Shri Vishnu, Shri Ganapati and Shri Shankar). The entrance is flanked by two life-size black-stone elephants and the temple has two distinctive deepstambhas. The Dussehra festival is celebrated from Ashwin Shuddha Pratipada to Poornima and draws around 25,000 devotees. CSV TOWN CORRECTED: the temple is at Parshem (Parcem) village, about 7 km from Pernem — not in Pernem town. Coordinates are approximate (for Parshem village).

name: Shri Bhagavati Temple
town_description: Parshem (also spelled Parcem) is a small village in Pernem taluka of North Goa, about 7 km from Pernem town. Set amid palm groves and laterite countryside inland from the north Goa coast, it is a quiet agricultural village whose main claim to fame is the ancient Shri Bhagavati temple complex by the main road.

travel.airport: Goa International Airport (Dabolim), about 55 km (verify); Manohar International Airport (Mopa) is closer (verify)
travel.road: On the main road at Parshem, about 5.8 km from the Pernem bus stand
